description: A light, clinical/biotech dashboard aesthetic built on soft cards, translucent 3D anatomical renders, thin-weight display numerals, and calm blue/neutral color accents. Optimized for health-monitoring and diagnostic dashboards.

illustration.anatomical_render_tone: monochrome navy/slate translucent x-ray style, NOT flat color
illustration.flat_icon_illustration_tone: saturated realistic color (e.g. red lungs), used sparingly for a single focal graphic per card

stat_display_number.note: thin/light weight for emphasis numerals, NOT bold

layout.grid_structure: 3-column dashboard grid: left column (stacked stat cards), center column (large focal illustration/visualization card, full height), right column (stacked stat + list cards)
layout.responsive_behavior: columns stack vertically below ~1024px; center focal card always keeps priority/top position on mobile

card.header_row: icon-chip + title on left, expand/maximize icon on right, spaced with flex justify-between

icon_chip.background: accent.primary_blue_light or status_*_bg depending on context
icon_chip.icon_style: thin 1.5px stroke line icons, no fill

stat_gauge_card.structure: semi-circular arc gauge behind a large thin-weight numeral, small limit/threshold label above the arc
stat_gauge_card.arc_fill_color: chart.gauge_fill or status color if out-of-range

sparkline_card.structure: large percentage/number top-left, small trend line/area chart bottom filling card width, 2-3 highlighted data-point pills floating above the line showing key values
sparkline_card.line_style: smooth curve, 2px stroke, gradient fill beneath
sparkline_card.highlight_pill: small rounded pill with % value, colored by status (red for low/alert, blue/neutral for normal)

data_table_card.header_row: icon-chip + title left, primary pill button right (e.g. 'View Records')
data_table_card.row_style: checkbox + date + label + category badge, divided by 1px hairline borders, zebra-free (white rows only)
data_table_card.category_badge: text-only colored label (no pill background) e.g. orange 'Moderate', green 'Normal', blue 'Mild'

list_card.structure: grouped by day/section label (muted small caps), each row = time chip + label + trailing icon chip
list_card.time_chip: rounded pill, colored background matches urgency/type (red = today/urgent, blue = scheduled)

focal_illustration_card.structure: large centered 3D or semi-transparent anatomical render floating with soft radial glow/vignette behind it, no hard card border around the illustration itself, illustration bleeds toward card edges
focal_illustration_card.toggle_control: pill-shaped segmented toggle centered at bottom edge of illustration (e.g. '<< 3D View >>') with chevron affordances indicating more views are swipeable

motion_guidelines.card_hover: subtle lift: shadow increases slightly, no scale transform
motion_guidelines.chart_update: smooth line/arc transitions (300-500ms ease-out) when values change, avoid abrupt jumps
motion_guidelines.toggle_switch: sliding pill indicator animates between segmented options (150-250ms)

imagery_guidelines.hero_illustration_style: translucent, x-ray/wireframe or ghosted 3D anatomical render in cool monochrome tones; conveys 'scientific/medical scan' feeling rather than literal photorealism
imagery_guidelines.supporting_icon_illustration_style: small, single flat-colored realistic icon (e.g. an organ icon) used only in compact stat cards, never as the hero visual
imagery_guidelines.avoid: cartoonish icons, heavy drop shadows, saturated multi-color illustrations, stock photography of people

organ_visualization_spec.applies_to: Digital Liver hero 3D visualization (center focal card)

base_shell.material_approach: semi-transparent shell (opacity 0.25-0.4) with Fresnel rim-brightening so edges read brighter than the face-on surface, consistent with the reference screenshot's ribcage/spine render
base_shell.surface_treatment: subtle wireframe or scan-line overlay optional, to reinforce 'x-ray' read

vessel_network.style: bright red, high-contrast branching vessel lines visible through the translucent shell — the classic contrast-dye angiography look
vessel_network.color: #E63946 to #FF4D4D, emissive/additive so it glows through the shell rather than sitting flat on top
vessel_network.geometry_approach: procedural branching tube mesh (recursive L-system or simple randomized bifurcating curves) rooted at one entry point (portal vein analog), OR a baked vein-pattern emissive texture mapped onto the shell if time is short
vessel_network.density: sparse-to-medium — a few primary branches with 2-3 levels of forking reads clearly at dashboard scale; do not over-branch or it becomes visual noise
vessel_network.always_visible: vessels stay visible and red at all health states — they are the constant reference structure against which shell damage color is judged

damage_progression.overview: Two visually distinct, independently-driven degradation passes layered on the same shell, matching the two mechanisms in the underlying lobule simulation. They must read as different patterns, not just different speeds of the same effect.
damage_progression.healthy_state: shell reads cool translucent blue/slate, vessels bright clean red, no dark patches, no mottling

acute_pathway.driver: uniform `acuteDamage` in [0,1], bound to `frac_necrotic` from the simulation
acute_pathway.visual_signature: ORIGIN-ANCHORED, SPREADING wave — patches begin at one or a few localized points and grow outward over time, never appear uniformly across the whole shell at once
acute_pathway.implementation_approach: map each lobule's grid position to UV coordinates on the shell mesh. Identify the highest-damage lobule cluster's centroid each frame and bias the noise field's threshold/offset so patch growth is concentrated near that UV region first, expanding outward as `acuteDamage` rises — do not use a spatially-uniform noise field for this pathway
acute_pathway.color_progression: slate → dull amber/brown at the wavefront edge → near-black/dark-red at the fully necrotic core, consistent with severe_damage tones below
acute_pathway.vessel_response: vessels within/near the spreading patch dim or flicker (impaired local flow); vessels elsewhere stay bright red and unaffected — this contrast is what sells 'localized' to the eye

chronic_pathway.driver: uniform `chronicLoad` in [0,1], bound to `mean(chronic_load)` across all lobules from the simulation
chronic_pathway.visual_signature: DIFFUSE, GRID-WIDE dulling — mottled patches appear gradually and roughly simultaneously across most of the shell's surface, with no single origin point and no directional spreading
chronic_pathway.implementation_approach: use a spatially-flat/uniform noise field (no UV-position bias, unlike the acute pathway) thresholded against `chronicLoad`, so patches pop up scattered across the whole shell at a similar rate rather than growing from one point
chronic_pathway.color_progression: slate → uniform dull amber-brown haze across most of the surface → deeper brown/dark-red mottling at high `chronicLoad`, visually distinct from the acute pathway's near-black necrotic core (keep chronic tones warmer/browner, acute tones darker/blacker, so the two are distinguishable even when both are present)
chronic_pathway.vessel_response: vessels desaturate slightly and uniformly across the whole network as `chronicLoad` rises, rather than the acute pathway's localized dimming — represents generalized reduced flow, not a local blockage

damage_progression.combined_state_handling: if both pathways are simultaneously non-zero, render both passes layered (acute wave visually on top / higher contrast, chronic haze as an underlying tone across the rest of the shell) — do not average or blend them into one uniform value, since collapsing them defeats the purpose of showing two distinct mechanisms

failure_state_event.trigger: on `failedAt` being set by the simulation (either failureType 'acute' or 'chronic', per verdict.ts)
failure_state_event.visual_event: a brief, unmissable transition distinct from ordinary progression: a fast color pulse toward deep black/red across the affected pattern (acute: the spread wave; chronic: the diffuse haze), then freeze all shell animation and playback at that frame — do not continue idle-animating a 'dead' shell
failure_state_event.on_shell_label: small text overlay near the shell, matching VerdictCard's failure badge wording ('LIVER FAILURE — centrilobular necrosis' or 'CHRONIC LIVER FAILURE — cumulative dosing exceeded regenerative capacity'), styled per badge_label typography token
failure_state_event.distinctness_requirement: this must look like a discrete event the viewer notices happening, not just the natural endpoint of the shell continuing to darken — use motion_guidelines.chart_update easing but compress it into a sharper, faster transition (~150-250ms) than the ordinary gradual progression, similar to motion_guidelines.toggle_switch timing

damage_progression.implementation_note: drive all patch growth with noise fields compared against thresholds derived from the driving uniform(s), never a flat opacity/color lerp — a uniform tint looks like a filter, patchy noise-driven damage looks like pathology. The acute/chronic distinction lives entirely in HOW the noise field is spatially structured (origin-biased vs. uniform), not in color alone.

accessibility_notes.contrast: ensure thin-weight large numerals maintain sufficient contrast against white card backgrounds (#111318 on #FFFFFF passes; avoid using text.muted for primary data values)
accessibility_notes.color_only_status: pair every status color (success/warning/danger) with a text label, not color alone
